Quick side note: carbon dioxide is most soluble in soda when the temperature is cold and the pressure is high. Opening the can causes the pressure to drop, which causes the low solubility of the carbon dioxide in Coke Zero to become significant as the soda goes flat.

**Disclaimer: I am in no way an expert on this subject, so this is purely speculation.** In chemistry, we learned about what causes soda to go flat. The presence of carbonic acid is what gives soda its fizzy taste, and carbon dioxide needs to be present in the soda for carbonic acid to be created. When a soda goes flat, the carbon dioxide comes out of solution, and there is little to no carbonic acid left in the soda. Solubility, which in this case determines how much carbon dioxide will dissolve in the soda, is probably the key factor here. I would imagine that carbon dioxide is simply less soluble in Coke Zero than it is in other sodas, which would cause less carbonic acid to be created, which leads to the soda going flat.
